transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Time: 10:00 AM PT (17:00 UTC)
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen, Maya Patel, Luis Romero, Sofia Nguyen, Evan Park + All employees (virtual)

Summary:
- Company update: ARR growth, hires, runway update, focus on Private and Dedicated product motion.
- Product: new autoscaling and quantization recommendations, model routing policy improvements.
- Engineering: runtime perf wins, kernel selection improvements, reduced p99 latency on 512-token workloads.
- Ops: upcoming SOC 2 Type II re-audit and audit readiness checklist.
- Q&A and next steps: share slides, publish dedicated benchmarks, follow-up deep dives with platform teams.

Topics:
- Business metrics and hiring
- Product roadmap: Dedicated, Private, Optimize features
- Performance highlights: kernels, batching, KV cache improvements
- Security & compliance timeline
- Customer stories & wins

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, good morning, good afternoon, thanks for joining the September all-hands. uh, big agenda but we'll keep it tight. uh if you're in APAC thanks for staying late.
[00:18] Avery: quick call-outs: great quarter, we're up 42% ARR q/q, expansion across mid-market, renewals trending strong. runway is extended after Series C bridge, we are prioritizing hires in infra and enterprise sales.
[00:35] Maya: thanks avery. on the product side we shipped the new autoscaler for Dedicated, it's in internal beta with three customers, seeing better utilization and predictable throughput. there are still kinks — burst behavior needs tuning — but the telemetry is there.
[00:52] Luis: the runtime work shipped last sprint: new kernel selector landed, and we saw p95 drop by about 18% on the 512 token benchmark. also the kv cache improvements cut cold-start token cost around, uh, 12% on our internal workloads.
[01:12] Sofia: wanted to highlight Redwood Optimize — the recommendation engine is now surfacing quantization profiles per model by workload. early signals show customers can save 20-40% per token for high-throughput embedding pipelines.
[01:30] Evan: and devrel is pushing a benchmark repo and quickstart for Dedicated perf testing, folks can self-serve and run the same tests we ran, that'll be in the docs by next week. link will be posted in #announcements.
[01:49] Employee 1: quick q, are we seeing any major churn with hosted customers moving to Dedicated?
[01:55] Sofia: good q — it's mixed. some high-throughput customers want Dedicated for cost predictability, others stick with hosted for ops simplicity. our routing policies let us offer fallbacks so apps don't outage when dedicated pools are saturated.
[02:10] Avery: to add, our thesis is serving > model ownership. we want customers to focus on product dev not infra; that means giving predictable SLAs, cost levers, and good docs.
[02:26] Employee 2: any timeline for on-prem private offering GA?
[02:30] Maya: private GA is targeted for Q1 next year, current progress is on the control plane security hardening and KMS/HSM integrations. some early pilots in regulated industries are moving well but we need to harden installer UX.
[02:47] Luis: note, the on-prem package needs better hardware detection — there were a few quirks in GPU discovery in last pilot, those are being fixed.
[03:02] Avery: on the business front, channel partnerships in EU are ramping; we signed two MSP partners for private hosting. that's helpful for data residency asks.
[03:18] Maya: ops update: SOC 2 Type II re-audit scheduled in mid-October. we need team help for evidence collection: incident logs, onboarding docs, and last year's change logs. I'll send an audit readiness checklist.
[03:34] Employee 3: will SSO/SAML changes affect current customers?
[03:38] Sofia: minorly, we will roll out SAML improvements with migration docs. no forced downtime expected.
[03:45] Evan: quick demo note — function calling and streaming improvements are GA on hosted, and we'll port streaming improvements to Dedicated next quarter. streaming had a few edge cases with micro-batching, which were fixed by changing the flush heuristics.
[04:05] Audience: applause emoji in chat (inaudible)
[04:10] Avery: customer stories — shoutout to Kinara Health, who implemented our model caching to reduce token spend by about 30% while keeping latency SLOs. also big win: a finance customer finished POC and moved to Dedicated commit.
[04:28] Employee 4: question on competitors — mentioned openai in the board notes; how do we position about quality vs cost?
[04:34] Avery: we position on predictable economics and deployment flexibility. yes, some competitors have leading base models but we win on operational controls, observability, and cost transparency.
[04:48] Maya: technical note — our kernel selection is now model-aware, we pick lower-precision kernels for compatible ops (quant friendly) and fallback otherwise. this reduces thermal throttling on some GPU types.
[05:05] Luis: perf caveat: for very long context (2k+ tokens) some models still have higher p99; we're working on KV cache evictions and chunked attention to mitigate.
[05:22] Avery: on hiring — we added 18 folks last quarter, mainly infra, product, and CSM. still hiring for reliability engineers and sales to support Dedicated.
[05:34] Employee 5: roadmap ask — can we get a deeper session specifically on rollout policies and A/B testing for model variants?
[05:39] Sofia: yes, we'll schedule a product deep dive for platform teams; that'll include canaries, automatic fallback policies, and metrics to watch.
[05:52] Evan: devrel will run office hours next Wednesday for folks running the Dedicated quickstart. drop in with issues.
[06:00] Q&A section (rapid fire):
[06:01] Employee 6: compliance question — data residency in APAC, are we cert'd?
[06:05] Maya: not regionally certified yet; partners are helping with regional footprint. some customers host private to satisfy residency.
[06:14] Employee 7: product question — when will the routing by cost-tier be available?
[06:18] Sofia: routing by policy for cost tiers is in alpha, expect public beta in Q4.
[06:24] Employee 8: misc — curious about pricing changes?
[06:27] Avery: no broad price increases planned; we will keep usage pricing competitive but introduce more granular options like burst credits and committed discounts for Dedicated.
[06:39] Maya: ops note — audit logs improvements for Private customers include per-request tracing and longer retention (configurable).
[06:49] Luis: quick tech foible in the transcript: we sometimes see K V cache spelled differently in docs, we'll standardize on "KV cache".
[06:59] Sofia: final plug — Redwood Optimize will trial customers with targeted cost-savings recommendations; product team will reach out to pilot customers next week.
[07:12] Avery: ok final recap: slides will be posted in the internal drive, Maya will send SOC2 checklist, SE/devrel will publish Dedicated benchmarks and quickstart, Product will schedule rollout deep dive.
[07:26] Avery: thanks everyone, we hit our OKRs for the quarter, keep shipping, let's take Qs offline.
[07:34] Crowd noise / applause (virtual)
